resources.string: "Share your code or QR to receive a request."
"Waiting for the other device to accept"
"Register a device, link it to your user directory and add call screens."
"Disabled or blocked · open the sample to check requests"
"This removes recent calls and saved participant names."
"Enter a valid device code or scan a DirectStream SDK pairing QR."
"This call request is no longer available."
"Unlock the device to accept this call."
"Join my video call: webrtcstream://pair/%1$s. I will approve your request."
"Your call continues with audio. Video pauses away from the call screen."
"Your recent devices will appear here. Names are supplied by the other device’s host app."
"Compare this verification value. Camera and audio start only after acceptance."
"Not allowed · incoming audio still works. Changes apply to the next call."
"All devices can receive requests. You choose whether to accept every call."
"Stored privately on this device. Clearing history does not end your call or reset the device code."
"Two-way video and audio, with explicit acceptance for every call."
"Configuration is supplied by the host app. Local validation does not check service reachability or guarantee call connectivity."
"Default provider: Firebase Spark and Cloudflare Workers Free. Developers configure their own projects; custom providers can use other infrastructure."
"TURN is disabled by default. Restrictive networks may prevent direct calls. Free-service quotas and Android notification policies can interrupt availability."
"Display names do not verify identity. Device codes locate clients; accepting a request authorizes the call."

"Use the ready-made Compose flow or observe typed state and send commands from your own interface. Install DirectStream 1.0.0 from Maven Central; one starter dependency includes the runtime, Compose UI and Firebase provider."
"Include the SDK modules and their implementation dependencies from this repository."
"Provide your public Firebase client configuration and HTTPS Worker URL. Never include server credentials in Android code."
"Use your MaterialTheme. Forward activity visibility with client.setVisible(true/false); do not dispose on rotation or backgrounding."
"The host forwards push delivery. The SDK validates each request before showing an alert; accepting still requires the call UI and permissions."
"For the default provider, enable Firebase anonymous authentication, publish the supplied RTDB rules and deploy the Worker. Put the Google service-account key only in Worker secrets."
"See README.md and the docs directory in this repository for the complete manifest, lifecycle, permission, custom-provider and teardown examples."
"Only accept if you expected this call. A display name does not verify identity."
"Camera and microphone start after you accept. Unlocking may be required."
"The old code and pending requests stop working. An active call continues."
"Continue without sending audio? You can still hear the other participant. Microphone permission takes effect on your next call."
"Camera access is required. On Android 17, also allow Nearby devices / local network access."
"Notifications are disabled. Open the app to check incoming calls; ongoing-call controls may not appear in the notification drawer."
Revoke your current code and create a new one. Share the new code or QR to receive future calls.
Your old code, QR and pairing link will stop accepting new requests. Pending incoming requests will be cancelled. An already approved call will continue.

"Initialize one process client in Application. Retrieve it later with DirectStreamClient.current(); this is the calls instance used in the examples. Your app owns login, its user/device database and recipient selection. The SDK owns call UI and media."
"Use io.github.orthoepiccrown0:directstream:1.0.0 from Maven Central. The showcase consumes the same published SDK. Hilt is a host choice and is not required by the SDK."

"Initialize before login with participantName = null and your configured provider. Retrieve the same client using DirectStreamClient.current(), or inject it into your UI and messaging service. Initialize even on a push-only process start."

"Initialization does not register or start media. After login, call activate(participantName = displayName), handle CallResult and observe registration.device. Update a profile name with updateParticipantName; null clears only the label. Deactivate on logout to clear the stored name and revoke registration. The host separately removes its own user/device mapping."

"Store the code with your authenticated user and stable installation ID in your own database. Support multiple devices per user and sync changed codes. The host server must verify ownership; a client-supplied code alone is not proof. Run the collector in the signed-in user scope."

"Resolve the recipient through your authenticated directory and let the user select an available device. Every call still needs the recipient’s approval. The bundled provider supports one receiver at a time, not user-level ringing on all devices."

"Wrap your navigation in DirectStreamHost. It owns permission preflight, lifecycle and incoming, waiting and in-call presentation. Your app supplies contacts and callbacks. Every call still requires acceptance."

"Forward incoming messages, the existing startup FCM token and token changes through handlePush and updatePushToken. Typed results distinguish unrelated, stale and retryable work. Incoming calls are core. Full-screen access depends on host declarations and platform policy. The Compose host binds lifecycle; background audio continues while video pauses."

"Confirm before regeneration. The provider revokes the previous code and pending incoming requests while preserving approved calls. Update your user/device directory with the new value. Remove old account bindings and revoke the code when changing the device’s signed-in user."

"QR codes, scanner entry, pairing links and the sample Home screen are showcase tools. Host-assigned participant names are SDK metadata and can change after login. Your product owns its authenticated user/device directory and recipient selection."

"A named Firebase app maintains the SDK installation identity separately from the host Firebase Auth user. Your application owns user authentication and its user/device directory. The SDK exposes registration changes and a short-lived ownership proof for backend verification; it does not bind business accounts automatically."

"Deploy the v1 Worker with its D1 coordination database and participant-restricted Firebase rules. For a fresh setup, create the D1 schema and ready marker before enabling requests; see README.md. Public Firebase configuration and Worker URL are host-owned. Incoming calls are core; push messages and token changes are always forwarded by the host. Configure customer-owned TURN for production connectivity; the free demo remains direct-only until configured. Server credentials stay outside Android code."

Explore every sample screen without a second device. Examples use synthetic data and never start a call, camera, microphone or network request. Call controls are simulated.
Device code, QR, recent attempts and host-assigned names.
Manual code entry. Real scanning is available from Home → Call a device.
Verification value, request expiry and cancellation.
Caller identity, verification and explicit acceptance.
Video layout, mute, audio routing and expandable diagnostics.
Audio-only presentation while the other camera is paused.
Receive-only audio with microphone controls disabled.
SDK overview, permissions, setup status and sample data.
Settings before a provider is configured.
Host initialization, device mapping and ready-made call UI.
Applies to the next call. Changes never alter the current or pending call.
Peer compatibility is unknown until the next approved call.
Choose a mutually compatible codec, prioritizing hardware support.
Reject incompatible calls instead of using a different codec.
Not exposed by the bundled WebRTC engine.
Video calls include two-way audio. Audio-only calls require newer service support.
Incoming channel is silent or low priority · the screen may not wake. Check channel settings.
Allow full-screen call alerts to show the incoming screen when your phone is locked. Android controls presentation; unlocked phones normally show a call banner.
